lessons.name: Multiplication word problems with factors up to 10

contents.html: There are 3 people on each relay race team. Each person runs 2 laps. How many laps long is the relay race?
There are 3 people on each relay race team. Each person runs 2 laps. How many laps long is the relay race?

content.html:
There are 3 people who each run 2 laps. Multiply:

3 × 2 = 6

The relay race is 6 laps long.

contents.html: Jill planted 4 types of trees in her orchard. She planted 5 of each type of tree. How many trees did Jill plant in the orchard?
Jill planted 4 types of trees in her orchard. She planted 5 of each type of tree. How many trees did Jill plant in the orchard?

content.html:
There are 4 types of trees and 5 of each type. Multiply:

4 × 5 = 20

Jill planted 20 trees in the orchard.

contents.html: There are 4 rows of seats in the classroom. Each row has 2 seats. How many seats are there in all?
There are 4 rows of seats in the classroom. Each row has 2 seats. How many seats are there in all?

content.html:
There are 4 rows of 2 seats. Multiply:

4 × 2 = 8

There are 8 seats in all.

contents.html: Reggie bought 5 bags of candy. There were 2 pieces of candy in each bag. How many pieces of candy did Reggie buy?
Reggie bought 5 bags of candy. There were 2 pieces of candy in each bag. How many pieces of candy did Reggie buy?

content.html:
There were 5 bags, each of which had 2 pieces of candy. Multiply:

5 × 2 = 10

Reggie bought 10 pieces of candy.

contents.html: A jeweler made 5 ruby necklaces. She used 5 rubies to make each necklace. How many rubies did the jeweler use?
A jeweler made 5 ruby necklaces. She used 5 rubies to make each necklace. How many rubies did the jeweler use?

content.html:
There were 5 necklaces, each of which had 5 rubies. Multiply:

5 × 5 = 25

The jeweler used 25 rubies.

contents.html: A summer camp has 3 cabins, and 4 campers can sleep in each cabin. How many campers can the cabins hold?
A summer camp has 3 cabins, and 4 campers can sleep in each cabin. How many campers can the cabins hold?

content.html:
There are 3 cabins, each of which can hold 4 campers. Multiply:

3 × 4 = 12

The cabins can hold 12 campers.

contents.html: Maddie's town built a new fence. Each section of the fence has 2 fence posts. The fence has 5 sections. How many fence posts does the fence have in all?
Maddie's town built a new fence. Each section of the fence has 2 fence posts. The fence has 5 sections. How many fence posts does the fence have in all?

content.html:
There are 5 sections, each of which has 2 fence posts. Multiply:

2 × 5 = 10

The fence has 10 fence posts in all.

contents.html: Jada bought 4 packages of T-shirts. Each package contained 4 T-shirts. How many T-shirts did Jada buy in total?
Jada bought 4 packages of T-shirts. Each package contained 4 T-shirts. How many T-shirts did Jada buy in total?

content.html:
There were 4 packages, each of which had 4 T-shirts. Multiply:

4 × 4 = 16

Jada bought 16 T-shirts.

contents.html: Sophia bought 2 packs of light bulbs. Each pack had 2 light bulbs. How many light bulbs did Sophia buy?
Sophia bought 2 packs of light bulbs. Each pack had 2 light bulbs. How many light bulbs did Sophia buy?

content.html:
There were 2 packs of 2 light bulbs. Multiply:

2 × 2 = 4

Sophia bought 4 light bulbs.

contents.html: A city has 2 parking spots on each block. How many parking spots are there on 4 blocks?
A city has 2 parking spots on each block. How many parking spots are there on 4 blocks?

content.html:
There are 2 parking spots on each of 4 blocks. Multiply:

2 × 4 = 8

There are 8 parking spots on 4 blocks.

contents.html: For a joke competition, 3 people each told 5 jokes. How many jokes were told in all?
For a joke competition, 3 people each told 5 jokes. How many jokes were told in all?

content.html:
There were 3 people who each told 5 jokes. Multiply:

3 × 5 = 15

15 jokes were told in all.

contents.html: Pam bought 2 T-shirts at a sidewalk sale. Each T-shirt cost $3. How much money did Pam spend?
Pam bought 2 T-shirts at a sidewalk sale. Each T-shirt cost $3. How much money did Pam spend?

content.html:
There were 2 T-shirts, each of which cost $3. Multiply:

2 × $3 = $6

Pam spent $6.

contents.html: A pet store has 5 tanks of fish. There are 4 fish in each tank. How many fish does the pet store have in all?
A pet store has 5 tanks of fish. There are 4 fish in each tank. How many fish does the pet store have in all?

content.html:
There are 5 tanks, each of which has 4 fish. Multiply:

5 × 4 = 20

The pet store has 20 fish.

contents.html: At a local school, 5 students are putting on a puppet show. Each student made 3 puppets for the show. How many puppets are there in all?
At a local school, 5 students are putting on a puppet show. Each student made 3 puppets for the show. How many puppets are there in all?

content.html:
There are 5 students who each made 3 puppets. Multiply:

5 × 3 = 15

There are 15 puppets in all.

contents.html: Shelby bought 4 packages of paper towels. There were 3 rolls in each package. How many rolls of paper towels did Shelby buy?
Shelby bought 4 packages of paper towels. There were 3 rolls in each package. How many rolls of paper towels did Shelby buy?

content.html:
There were 4 packages, each of which had 3 rolls of paper towels. Multiply:

4 × 3 = 12

Shelby bought 12 rolls of paper towels.

contents.html: There are 3 students in the school's writing club. Last year, each student in the club wrote 3 stories. How many stories were written in all?
There are 3 students in the school's writing club. Last year, each student in the club wrote 3 stories. How many stories were written in all?

content.html:
There are 3 students who each wrote 3 stories. Multiply:

3 × 3 = 9

9 stories were written in all.

contents.html: An aquarium has 3 tanks of sharks. Each tank has 2 sharks. How many sharks are there in the aquarium?
An aquarium has 3 tanks of sharks. Each tank has 2 sharks. How many sharks are there in the aquarium?

content.html:
There are 3 tanks, each of which holds 2 sharks. Multiply:

3 × 2 = 6

There are 6 sharks in the aquarium.

contents.html: A city wants to plant 4 trees on each block. How many trees will the city need for 2 blocks?
A city wants to plant 4 trees on each block. How many trees will the city need for 2 blocks?

content.html:
There are 4 trees each for 2 blocks. Multiply:

4 × 2 = 8

The city will need 8 trees for 2 blocks.

contents.html: Ann's sticker collection fills 4 pages in her sticker book. There are 5 stickers on each page. How many stickers are in Ann's collection?
Ann's sticker collection fills 4 pages in her sticker book. There are 5 stickers on each page. How many stickers are in Ann's collection?

content.html:
There are 4 pages, each of which has 5 stickers. Multiply:

4 × 5 = 20

There are 20 stickers in Ann's collection.

contents.html: Lindsey has 2 shelves of dolls in her room. There are 4 dolls on each shelf. How many dolls are there in total?
Lindsey has 2 shelves of dolls in her room. There are 4 dolls on each shelf. How many dolls are there in total?

content.html:
There are 2 shelves with 4 dolls each. Multiply:

2 × 4 = 8

There are 8 dolls in total.

contents.html: At a local school, 5 students each wrote 2 letters to students in another country. How many letters were written in all?
At a local school, 5 students each wrote 2 letters to students in another country. How many letters were written in all?

content.html:
There are 5 students who each wrote 2 letters. Multiply:

5 × 2 = 10

10 letters were written in all.

contents.html: There are 3 students in the poetry club. Last year, each student wrote 4 poems. How many poems did the students in the club write in all?
There are 3 students in the poetry club. Last year, each student wrote 4 poems. How many poems did the students in the club write in all?

content.html:
There are 3 students who each wrote 4 poems. Multiply:

3 × 4 = 12

There were 12 poems in all.

contents.html: Tessa made 5 picture collages. She used 5 pictures in each collage. How many pictures did Tessa use in all?
Tessa made 5 picture collages. She used 5 pictures in each collage. How many pictures did Tessa use in all?

content.html:
There were 5 collages, each of which had 5 pictures. Multiply:

5 × 5 = 25

Tessa used 25 pictures in all.

contents.html: Brad bought 4 boxes of chocolates. There were 4 chocolates in each box. How many chocolates did Brad buy?
Brad bought 4 boxes of chocolates. There were 4 chocolates in each box. How many chocolates did Brad buy?

content.html:
There were 4 boxes, each of which had 4 chocolates. Multiply:

4 × 4 = 16

Brad bought 16 chocolates.

contents.html: A candy company puts 4 gumdrops in each bag. How many gumdrops will the company need to fill 2 bags?
